::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#sol-local-vs-global-min}

1. Since $f(1) = 1 - 3 = -2$,

   $$
   \ba
   f(x) - f(1) &= x^3 - 3x + 2
   \\ &= (x - 1)(x^2 + x - 2)
   \\ &= (x - 1)(x - 1)(x + 2)
   \\ &= (x - 1)^2 (x + 2).
   \ea
   $$

2. For $x \in (0, 2)$,
   $(x - 1)^2 \ge 0$ and $x + 2 > 0$,
   so their product is at least $0$.
   By part 1, $f(x) - f(1) \ge 0$,
   that is, $f(x) \ge f(1)$.

3. $f(-3) = -27 + 9 = -18$.
   Since $-18 < -2 = f(1)$,
   $f(1)$ is not the smallest value of $f$ on $\reals$.

4. No.
   For each $n \ge 2$,
   $f(-n) = -n^3 + 3n = -n(n^2 - 3) \le -n$,
   so no value of $f$ is smaller than all the others:
   for any $x$, picking $n \ge 2$ with $-n < f(x)$
   gives $f(-n) < f(x)$.

:::

:::
